title: 1H: Build the Map
hook: What structure and swings are actually relevant?

launchpad.outcome: Carry your 4H read onto the 1H, mark the previous 1H swing high and low, name the 1H structure, and explain how it relates to the 4H.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What structure and swings are actually relevant?

slides.headline: Carry the 4H story down and build the 1H map.
slides.line: The 1-hour chart shows the detail inside the 4H range. Your job is to find which structure and swings actually matter.

slides.headline: Bring your 4H read onto the 1H. Don’t start over.
slides.line: The 1H sits inside the 4H range, so everything you found on the 4H comes with you.

notes.text: 4H: bullish · lower area of the range · correcting

steps.text: The 4H swing high and 4H swing low come with you. They frame everything you see on the 1H.
You also bring the current 4H structure, the important 4H levels and the current HTF (higher timeframe) ICC phase.

slides.headline: Find the previous 1H swing high and swing low.
slides.line: Look for the major structural swings, not the smaller internal movements between them.

notes.text: 4H: bullish · lower area of the range · correcting

steps.text: These small wiggles are internal movements. They happen inside a bigger leg and don’t define the structure.
This is the previous 1H swing low. Price made a lower low here before bouncing.
This is the previous 1H swing high. Price turned lower from it, and it is trading between these two swings now.

slides.headline: Is the 1H bullish, bearish, consolidating, or transitioning?
slides.line: Name the 1H structure from its swings. Remember, it can temporarily move against the 4H direction.

cards.label: Consolidating
cards.sub: Price moves inside a range with no clear progress.

cards.label: Transitioning
cards.sub: Structure is changing through a market structure shift (MSS).

check.prompt: The 4H is bullish, but the 1H is making lower highs and lower lows. Can both be true?

options.label: No, one of them must be wrong
options.feedback: Both can be true. The 1H can temporarily move against the broader 4H direction.

options.label: Yes, the 1H can move against the 4H for a while
options.why: Right. The 1H can temporarily move against the 4H, so you read each one for what it is.

slides.headline: Mark only the levels that actually matter.
slides.line: Relevant levels are the previous 1H swing highs and lows, plus any nearby 4H levels.

notes.text: 4H: bullish · lower area of the range · correcting

steps.text: The previous 1H swing high and swing low are relevant structural levels.
The 4H swing high and swing low are higher timeframe levels, so they stay on your map too.
Not every high or low automatically becomes a trading level. These small internal swings don’t make the map.

check.prompt: A tiny internal high just formed on the 1H. Does it automatically become a trading level?

options.label: Yes, every high is a level
options.feedback: Not every high or low automatically becomes a trading level. Relevant levels come from the structure.

options.label: No, not every high or low becomes a level
options.why: Exactly. You map the previous 1H swings and nearby 4H levels, not every small wiggle.

slides.headline: How does the 1H relate to the 4H?
slides.line: Tap each scenario. Interpret the relationship instead of trading whichever chart looks strongest.

cards.label: Scenario A
cards.sub: 4H bullish, 1H bullish. Both timeframes support bullish conditions.

cards.label: Scenario B
cards.sub: 4H bullish, 1H bearish. The 1H may be correcting, or structure may be changing.

cards.label: Scenario C
cards.sub: 4H bearish, 1H bullish. The 1H may be a countertrend move.

check.prompt: The 4H is bearish, and the 1H just made a strong bullish move. What could the 1H be?

options.label: A countertrend move inside the bearish 4H
options.why: That’s Scenario C. The 1H may be a countertrend move, so you interpret it before doing anything.

options.label: A buy signal, because it looks strongest
options.feedback: Don’t automatically trade whichever timeframe looks strongest. First interpret how the 1H relates to the 4H.

slides.headline: If the first level breaks, don’t chase price.
slides.line: If price moves through the first relevant level and the next level is a 4H swing, you may keep observing that next level.

steps.text: The first relevant level is the 1H swing low. The next level below it is the 4H swing low.
Price moves through the first level. It has already been broken, so you don’t chase price.
The next level is a 4H swing, so you may continue observing it for a qualified Dayli ICC setup.

check.prompt: Price just broke through the 1H swing low you were watching. The next level is a 4H swing. What do you do?

options.label: Jump in now before price gets away
options.feedback: That’s chasing. Once the first level has already been broken, you don’t chase price.

options.label: Keep observing the 4H swing for a qualified setup
options.why: Yes. Because the next level is a 4H swing, you may keep observing it for a qualified Dayli ICC setup.

slides.headline: Put it all together into one complete 1H map.
slides.line: Tap each piece. Your 1H map isn’t complete until it holds all five.

steps.label: 4H context
steps.sub: The current 4H structure, swing high and low, and ICC phase.

steps.label: Previous 1H swings
steps.sub: The relevant 1H swing high and swing low.

steps.label: Nearby HTF levels
steps.sub: Any higher timeframe (4H) levels close to price.

steps.label: Where price is
steps.sub: Where price is trading right now on your map.

slides.title: Build this 1H map yourself.

tasks.say: This is your 4H read from the last lesson: bullish structure, lower area of the range, and price is correcting.

tasks.label: BUILD THE MAP →
tasks.say: Now carry it onto the 1H. You don’t start over: the 4H swing high and low stay on the chart.

tasks.prompt: Tap the previous relevant 1H swing high.
tasks.label: SWING HIGH

notes.0: That high is older. Price has built a whole new leg since, so it isn’t the previous swing high.
notes.2: That’s an earlier lower high. Which high came most recently, before price turned lower again?
notes.4: Real swing, but older. Look for the most recent swing high price turned down from.

tasks.why: That’s the most recent 1H swing high. Price turned lower from it.
tasks.say: Start with the swings. Find the most recent major 1H swing high, not an older one.

tasks.prompt: Now tap the previous relevant 1H swing low.
tasks.label: SWING LOW

notes.1: That low is older. Price has already traded below it, so it isn’t the previous swing low.
notes.3: Real swing, but price has already made a lower low since. Which low came last?

tasks.why: That’s the most recent 1H swing low. Price is trading just above it.

options.label: Bearish: lower highs and lower lows
options.why: Each 1H high and low is lower than the one before it.

options.label: Bullish: higher highs and higher lows
options.feedback: Follow the 1H swings from the left. Each high and each low is lower than the last.

options.label: Transitioning through an MSS
options.feedback: No lower high has been broken yet, so the 1H hasn’t shifted. It is still making lower highs and lower lows.

tasks.prompt: The 4H is bullish and the 1H is bearish. How does the 1H relate to the 4H?

options.label: The 1H may be correcting, or structure may be changing
options.why: That’s Scenario B. You interpret it and keep watching, without assuming either one.

options.label: The 4H is wrong now, so only the 1H matters
options.feedback: The 4H swings haven’t changed. The 1H can temporarily move against the 4H direction.

options.label: Trade whichever chart looks strongest
options.feedback: Don’t automatically trade whichever timeframe looks strongest. Interpret how they relate first.

tasks.value: Scenario B: 1H may be correcting, or structure may be changing

tasks.prompt: Which levels belong on your 1H map?

options.label: The previous 1H swing high and low, and nearby 4H levels
options.why: Right. Those are the relevant structural levels.

options.label: Every small high and low on the chart
options.feedback: Not every high or low automatically becomes a trading level. Map only the relevant structural levels.

tasks.prompt: Where is price trading on your 1H map right now?

options.label: Just above the 1H swing low, inside the 4H range
options.why: Yes. Price sits between the 1H swing high and low, close to the low, and still inside the 4H range.

options.label: Above the 1H swing high
options.feedback: Look again. Price is below the 1H swing high line.

options.label: Below the 4H swing low
options.feedback: The 4H swing low is still well below price. Price is inside the 4H range.

tasks.after: 1H MAP BUILT ✓ 4H context, 1H structure, the previous 1H swing high and low, nearby 4H levels, and where price is trading.

slides.outro: You built the map: what the 4H says, what the 1H is doing, and which levels actually matter.

slides.quote: Don’t start over on the 1H. Carry the 4H story down and map only what’s relevant.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what goes on a complete 1H map?
slides.modelAnswer: I carry over the 4H context: the 4H swing high and low, its structure, the important levels and the HTF ICC phase. Then I mark the previous 1H swing high and low, name the 1H structure, add nearby 4H levels, explain how the 1H relates to the 4H, and note where price is trading. If the first level breaks, I don’t chase; if the next level is a 4H swing, I may keep observing it for a qualified Dayli ICC setup.

takeaways: Carry the 4H read onto the 1H instead of starting over.
Mark the previous 1H swing high and low, not the small internal moves.
Name the 1H structure and interpret how it relates to the 4H.
If the first level breaks and the next is a 4H swing, observe it. Never chase.
remember: CARRY THE 4H DOWN. MAP ONLY WHAT MATTERS.
